title: Efficient Aggregation of Overidentified Staggered Triple-Difference Comparisons
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision reviews passed; the note achieved subfield novelty within its explicit constant-score-span scope, and the user elected to bank it as downgraded at the D-F boundary without entering formalization.
gap_reasons: The optimization and quadratic frontier are finite-dimensional GMM/SUR projection algebra, so the DDD-specific contribution is chiefly the shared-cell covariance mapping and its implementation rather than a new general efficiency theory.

This is too narrow for field or flagship status because it neither characterizes the full conditional-moment efficiency bound nor establishes uniform attainability, coverage, or inference for the estimated variance gap.
proof_attempt_summary: Stage D proved and reviewed the complete 11-node constant-score-span result: identification, conditional pointwise inference for the feasible joint estimator, an exact joint-versus-separate equality frontier and quadratic variance gap, and a bounded strict-gap family. Math and decision review passed, and the final general referee graded the result subfield, but the original broader semiparametric-efficiency ambition remained outside scope: no full conditional-moment EIF/bound, uniform learner attainability or coverage, or inference for the estimated gap was established. The user therefore banked the sound result as downgraded at the D-F boundary without formalization.
tldr: The causal aggregate \(\tau_\omega(Q)\) is identified by \(\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\). Conditional on supplied cross-fitted nuisance learners satisfying the displayed \(L_4(P_X)\) and product rates, an everywhere-defined clipped, projected, and ridged estimator has a pointwise Gaussian limit, consistent variance estimate, and Wald coverage. The incremental contribution is the staggered-DDD shared-cell score/covariance mapping, joint constant-span weighting for the prespecified scalar aggregate, the exact componentwise-versus-joint equality frontier and quadratic gap, a feasible descriptive loss diagnostic, and a bounded open nonzero-effect strict-gap family. Shared-unit covariance accounting and generic constrained-GMM/SUR quadratic algebra are prior art. Caron's subgroup-ATT semiparametric efficiency result concerns a distinct target; no full efficient influence function, semiparametric efficiency bound, uniform learner availability or coverage, or covariate-varying relative-precision result is claimed here.
gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna prove minimum variance within each group-time comparison block and then aggregate. Hsieh proves valid fixed-weight stacked-DDD inference with reused comparison units. Neither result checks whether blockwise optimization remains optimal for the final covariate-adjusted DDD aggregate when all admissible comparison-cohort scores are retained jointly.
fill: A separate supporting reduction identifies the full-data causal aggregate \(\tau_\omega(Q)\) with the displayed observed-data functional \(\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\). The joint incidence-constrained GMM construction then uses only \(P\), explicitly clipped propensities, a projected and ridged covariance, and an exact studentized interval. A bounded four-cell construction demonstrates feasibility when \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\). A score-specific argument uses foldwise independence, outcome, true-regression, and fitted-regression fourth-moment control, separate propensity and regression \(L_4\) errors, and their explicit \(o(n^{-1/2})\) product to derive asymptotic linearity and empirical score convergence. The entrywise covariance argument then derives operator-norm consistency. The if-and-only-if collapse frontier and quadratic variance-gap functional compare joint loading with the published componentwise plug-in without recasting shared-unit variance aggregation as new.
